sentences.text: The applicant is the husband of the deceased lady.
He has been convicted under Sections 302/498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and has been sentenced to suffer life imprisonment.
He now prays for suspension of sentence.
2. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the applicant particularly relied on the deposition of the girl child of the deceased and the applicant.

He also drew our attention to the statement of the girl child recorded under Section 164 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (corresponding to Section 183 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023).

The two versions are completely different Banat Mondal @ Banat Ali Mondal @ Binat vs Unknown on 23 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14983733/
1 and inconsistent with one another.

sentences.text: We further see that two other accused persons, who were stated to be present at the time of the alleged crime, have been acquitted by the learned Trial Judge.
4. Learned State Counsel strongly opposes the prayer and says that there are other witnesses who have supported the prosecution case.
However, in her usual fairness she does not dispute that the child witness is the only eyewitness.
She also relies on the post-mortem report.
5. We have seen the depositions of the witnesses.

We see from the statement of the child witness recorded under Section 164 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 and her deposition recorded before the learned Trial Court that the two are completely different.
In her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973, she said that her father came into the room in their house at night and strangulated her mother.
In her deposition the child witness clearly stated that her father, being the applicant herein, used to work in a jute mill and used to stay away for six months in a year.
After receiving the news of her mother's death, her father came to the Police Station.
This is not a case of minor inconsistency.
The child witness was not declared hostile by the prosecution.

We have noticed that the learned Trial Judge describe the child witness as the prosecution's "star witness" and the conviction was based primarily on the evidence of the child witness recorded before the learned Trial Court.
Such evidence prima facie does not support the prosecution case.

6. On an overall assessment of the facts and circumstances of the case and prima facie assimilation of the evidence on record, we are of the view that the applicant has been able to make out a prima facie arguable case for acquittal at the hearing of the appeal.
7. Accordingly, we are inclined to allow this application and we hereby do suspend the sentence of imprisonment of the applicant.

8. It is thus ORDERED that the applicant, namely, BANAT MONDAL @ BANAT ALI MONDAL @
BINAT MONDAL @ BINAT ALI MONDAL shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.
10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand), with two sureties of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand) each,
one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Murshidabad at Berhampore, subject to condition that the applicant shall remain within the geographical limits of the district of Murshidabad, except for the purpose of attending Court proceedings and shall report to the Inspector-in-Charge/Officer-in-Charge of Domkal Police Station, once in a month, until further orders and that the applicant shall be personally present or be represented through his learned Counsel before this Court on each and every date when the appeal is taken up for hearing and he will surrender before the Trial Court as and when called for in connection with the present appeal.
9. The operation of the order of conviction and sentence shall remain suspended till disposal of the appeal or until further orders, whichever is earlier.
